question_stem:
A ripple tank is used to demonstrate the interference of water waves.
Two dippers D1 and D2 produce coherent waves that have circular wavefronts, as illustrated in Fig. 5.1.

{{figure:figure_5_1}}

Fig. 5.1

The lines in the diagram represent crests. The waves have a wavelength of $6.0\text{ cm}$.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.part_stem: One condition that is required for an observable interference pattern is that the waves must be coherent.
parts.text: Describe how the apparatus is arranged to ensure that the waves from the dippers are coherent.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State one other condition that must be satisfied by the waves in order for the interference pattern to be observable.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Light from a lamp above the ripple tank shines through the water onto a screen below the tank. Describe one way of seeing the illuminated pattern more clearly.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: The speed of the waves is $0.40\text{ m s}^{-1}$. Calculate the period of the waves.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.part_stem:
Fig. 5.1 shows a point $X$ that lies on a crest of the wave from D1 and midway between two adjacent crests of the wave from D2.

For the waves at point $X$, state:

parts.label: (e)
parts.text: On Fig. 5.1, draw **one** line, at least $4\text{ cm}$ long, which joins points where only maxima of the interference pattern are observed.
